text: Sponges, which lack neurons entirely, can still propagate signals and coordinate behaviors such as closing their oscula through epithelial conduction.
explanation: True. Epithelial conduction propagates electrical or chemical signals through epithelial cells without neurons; in sponges it coordinates osculum closure in response to disturbance. Sally Leys's work on glass sponge electrical signaling established that such pre-neural coordination is real, demonstrating that coordinated signaling across a body does not require neurons.
